--- header_pre ---
#define j0 _j0
#define j1 _j1
#define jn _jn
#define y0 _y0
#define y1 _y1
#define yn _yn
#define gamma _gamma
#define lgamma _lgamma
#define tgamma _tgamma
#include <stddef.h>
#if defined(__APPLE__)
#include <OpenGL/gl.h>

#else
#define GL_GLEXT_PROTOTYPES

#include <GL/glext.h>
#include <GL/glu.h>
#include <GL/freeglut.h>
#endif
#include <math.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#undef j0
#undef j1
#undef jn
#undef y0
#undef y1
#undef yn
#undef gamma
#undef lgamma
#undef tgamma

#ifndef M_PI
#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846
#endif

static float g_angle = 0.0f;
static int   g_rotating = 0;

--- display_header ---
void display(void) {
  glLoadIdentity();
  glPushAttrib(GL_ALL_ATTRIB_BITS);
--- lights_pre_camera ---
  // Eye-space light positions, set before the camera transform.
  glLightfv(GL_LIGHT0, GL_POSITION, repl_glfloat4(0, 0, -1, 1));
--- camera ---
  // camera
  glTranslatef(0.0000f, 0.0000f, -6.0000f);
  glRotatef(10.0000f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
  glRotatef(0.0000f, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
  glTranslatef(-0.0000f, -0.0000f, -0.0000f);
--- header_post ---
--- render_state ---
  glEnable(GL_MULTISAMPLE);
  glDisable(GL_LINE_SMOOTH);
  float A[16], B[16], C[16];
--- source ---
  static float spin; // @tune  mask rotation, degrees

  // The window. Drawn twice - once as a stamp, once as an outline - so it
  // lives in a func and both passes are guaranteed to agree.
  maskWindow() {
    glPushMatrix();
      glRotatef(spin, 0, 0, 1);
      glBegin(GL_QUADS);
        glVertex3f(-0.75, -0.75, 0);
        glVertex3f(0.75, -0.75, 0);
        glVertex3f(0.75, 0.75, 0);
        glVertex3f(-0.75, 0.75, 0);
      glEnd();
    glPopMatrix();
  }

  // Stencil masking, minimum viable. Three passes over one shape:
  //   1. stamp it into the stencil buffer only - no color, no depth
  //   2. draw the payload where the stamp landed (GL_EQUAL, 1)
  //   3. trace the window edge with the test off, so the mask is visible
  // The stencil buffer itself does not render. Pass 3 is the only reason
  // you can tell where the window is - there is no stencil viewer yet, so
  // comment it out and the mask becomes guesswork. That is the point.

  glClearColor(0.05, 0.06, 0.08, 1);
  glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT | GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT);
  glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
  glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glEnable(GL_LIGHT0);
  glEnable(GL_NORMALIZE);
  glEnable(GL_COLOR_MATERIAL);
  glColorMaterial(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_AMBIENT_AND_DIFFUSE);
  glEnable(GL_STENCIL_TEST);

  spin = t * 20;

  // --- Pass 1: stamp -------------------------------------------------
  // Writes are off for color and depth, so the quad leaves no trace in
  // the frame. All it does is set stencil = 1 under its own footprint.
  // GL_ALWAYS means "never fail the comparison"; GL_REPLACE on the pass
  // branch is what actually writes ref (1) into the buffer.
  glColorMask(GL_FALSE, GL_FALSE, GL_FALSE, GL_FALSE);
  glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
  glStencilMask(0xFF); // decimal in; canonicalizes to 0xFF
  glStencilFunc(GL_ALWAYS, 1, 0xFF);
  glStencilOp(GL_KEEP, GL_KEEP, GL_REPLACE);
  maskWindow();

  // --- Pass 2: payload, clipped to the stamp -------------------------
  // GL_EQUAL, 1 admits only the stamped pixels. glStencilMask(0) makes
  // this pass read-only against the stencil buffer, so the teapot cannot
  // smear the mask it is being cut by.
  glColorMask(GL_TRUE, GL_TRUE, GL_TRUE, GL_TRUE);
  glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
  glStencilMask(0x00);
  glStencilFunc(GL_EQUAL, 1, 0xFF);
  glStencilOp(GL_KEEP, GL_KEEP, GL_KEEP);
  glColor3f(0.1, 0.95, 0.85);
  glPushMatrix();
    glRotatef(t * 35, 0, 1, 0);
    glutSolidTeapot(0.85);
  glPopMatrix();

  // --- Pass 3: show the window ---------------------------------------
  // Test off and depth off, so the outline always draws over everything -
  // including the part of the teapot the mask just removed.
  glDisable(GL_STENCIL_TEST);
  glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
  glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glColor3f(1, 0.85, 0.15);
  glLineWidth(2);
  glPolygonMode(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_LINE);
  maskWindow();
  glPolygonMode(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_FILL);
  glLineWidth(1);
  glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);

  // Things to try:
  //   - GL_EQUAL -> GL_NOTEQUAL in pass 2: the window becomes a hole.
  //   - GL_REPLACE -> GL_INCR in pass 1 and stamp twice from different
  //     angles; then GL_EQUAL, 2 in pass 2 keeps only the overlap.
  //   - drop glStencilMask(0) from pass 2 and watch the teapot chew
  //     through its own mask on the next frame.
